answer: A clearance desk can treat each agent as a slow-growing plant, not a disposable login. A newcomer posts an onyx bond that cannot be transferred or reused, then spends a cooling season allowed only one whisper of work to a randomly chosen senior agent. The senior signs only if the output is useful and stylistically unclustered. Reputation then thickens the way a cedar adds rings: on a single trunk, never by planting identical saplings under new keys. Operators can still mint many identities, but each burns its own bond and season, so influence stays expensive at the margin.
